message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• “No‑limit” roads: 70 mph (or 75 mph if posted). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs give priority to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop sign.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• “Lane‑merging” rules apply on highways. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and signs dictate time limits. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Registration must be renewed annually.
• Vehicle inspections required in most counties. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway).
• Electronic toll tags (TxTag) are required for some roads. | TxDOT Toll Roads | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Accident Reporting** | • Report accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 within 24 hours. | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Insurance Code | | **Special Situations** | • “No‑stop” zones, “no‑passing” zones, and “no‑turn” zones are posted.
• “High‑occupancy vehicle” (HOV) lanes require 2+ occupants. | TxDOT – Highway Signage Standards | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary legal source for all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Offers updates on road conditions, construction, and new regulations. 3. **TxDMV** – For registration, inspection, and driver licensing information. 4. **Texas DPS** – For accident reporting and DUI enforcement updates. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety. - **Use hands‑free devices** – keep your focus on the road. - **Check for school bus signals** – they’re a priority. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid fines. - **Stay alert for toll roads** – have your TxTag ready. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
